business: Winner Takes All — tournament software a venue pays for, to run its own competition night
target: Owners and managers of gaming cafés, pool halls, snooker parlours, PlayStation/console lounges and board-game cafés in Indian cities, who already run or want to run a regular competition night
where: India — tier 1 and tier 2 cities (Bengaluru, Pune, Kochi, Hyderabad, Indore, Coimbatore)

segments.name: Manager running the floor (not the owner)
Community league organiser, no venue of their own

behaviours.name: Runs it on paper now
behaviours.how: Draws the bracket on a whiteboard, keeps score in a notebook, has done it this way for years.

behaviours.name: WhatsApp organiser
behaviours.how: Runs everything through a WhatsApp group: entries, fixtures, results, arguments.

behaviours.name: Never run one
behaviours.how: Likes the idea of a league night but has never organised one and is not sure where to start.

behaviours.name: Tight on cash
behaviours.how: Counts every monthly subscription, has cancelled software before for not being used.

behaviours.name: Already pays for a POS/booking tool
behaviours.how: Used to paying a monthly SaaS fee for the venue, judges new tools against it.

behaviours.name: Tech-shy
behaviours.how: Does not want to learn new software, needs staff to pick it up in one shift.

behaviours.name: Burned by real-money apps
behaviours.how: Watched the 2025 gaming ban hit, wary of anything that looks like betting.

objections: I already do this on a whiteboard and it costs me nothing
A monthly fee for something I use four nights a month is hard to justify
My staff will not learn new software
Does this get more people through the door, or is it just admin?
Is this legal? It sounds like the betting apps that got banned
What happens when the internet drops mid-tournament?
I have no screen to put this on
Who pays the prize money — me?
habits: your busiest nights are Friday and Saturday and Tuesday is dead
you know your regulars by name and they ask when the next tournament is
you lost a whole evening last month to an argument about a disputed frame
you have a TV on the wall showing a muted cricket match
a sales rep calls you about software roughly once a fortnight
